name: New York — Midtown Manhattan
blurb: Times Square, Bryant Park and the Empire State Building on Manhattan's street grid. Brooklyn and Queens have been hit by weak tornadoes; Midtown never has.

name: London — The City
blurb: St Paul's, the Bank towers, London Bridge and the Shard along the Thames. The UK records many small tornadoes; traffic keeps left here.

name: Paris — Louvre and Île de la Cité
blurb: Six-storey stone blocks with zinc roofs on both banks of the Seine, from the Louvre to Notre-Dame.

name: Rome — Centro Storico
blurb: The Pantheon, Piazza Venezia, the Forum and the Colosseum in a maze of ochre masonry and terracotta roofs beside the Tiber.

name: Tokyo — Shinjuku
blurb: The skyscraper district west of Shinjuku Station surrounded by thousands of small buildings. Japan sees tornadoes most years; traffic keeps left here.

name: Rio de Janeiro — Centro
blurb: Avenida Rio Branco, Lapa and Central do Brasil. South of the equator the vortex spins clockwise. The hills around the centre are flattened in this model.
